title: Trace it: what shows, what comes back
idea: return vs print: for each snippet, say what APPEARS on screen and what the call HANDS BACK. Two separate questions.

exercises.prompt:
For this call, what APPEARS on screen?

def f(n):
    return n + 1

f(5)
exercises.explanation: return is silent and nothing prints the result, so the screen is blank. (It DID hand back 6 — but that's a separate question.)

exercises.prompt:
Same call — what does f(5) HAND BACK?

def f(n):
    return n + 1

f(5)
exercises.explanation: f(5) hands back 6. 'What appears' and 'what comes back' are two different questions — here: nothing shown, 6 returned.

exercises.prompt:
What APPEARS on screen?

def g(n):
    print(n + 1)

g(5)
exercises.explanation: print shows n + 1 = 6, so 6 appears. (But g hands back None — the other question.)

exercises.prompt:
Same call — what does g(5) HAND BACK?

def g(n):
    print(n + 1)

g(5)
exercises.explanation: g prints but has no return, so it hands back None. Shown: 6. Returned: None.

exercises.prompt: Match each sub-plan to what its call HANDS BACK.
exercises.explanation: Only a() returns a value. b() prints and returns None. c() computes but discards it, also None.

exercises.prompt:
What APPEARS (two lines)?

def h(n):
    print(n)
    return n * 10

print(h(3))
exercises.explanation: Inside h, print(n) shows 3 (first line). h returns 30; the outer print shows 30 (second line).

exercises.prompt: 'What appears on screen' and 'what the call hands back' are two separate questions you should answer one at a time.
exercises.explanation: Yes. A sub-plan can print one thing and return another. Tracing each separately avoids confusion.

exercises.prompt:
What does x hold?

def h(n):
    print(n)
    return n * 10

x = h(3)
exercises.explanation: h returns n * 10 = 30, so x is 30. (It also printed 3 on the way, but that doesn't affect x.)

exercises.prompt: REVIEW: which action is silent (shows nothing by itself)?
exercises.explanation: return is silent — it hands a value back without displaying it. print is the one that shows text.

options: Trace 'what shows' and 'what comes back' separately — they can differ
exercises.explanation: Keep the two questions apart. A sub-plan may show one value and return another — or show nothing while returning a lot.
